title: The Wee Bannock
note: A new, shortened adaptation of the cumulative Scottish tale. A bannock is a round, flat bread; in this version it is made with oatmeal.

rights.basis: Source edition published before 1929 and identified as public domain by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: A round oatmeal bannock rolls over green Scottish hills.
scenes: An old woman baked two fine oatmeal bannocks and set them by the fire. When her husband broke one in half for a taste, the other bannock took fright.
Down it dropped, across the floor it rolled, and out through the cottage door it flew.
The wee bannock rolled into a tailor’s house. The tailor came with his shears, his apprentices came with pins, and the tailor’s wife came with her cards for combing flax.
Round and round the fire they chased it. Zip! The bannock dodged them all and rolled back onto the road.
It escaped a weaver and his shuttle, a woman making butter, a miller dusty with flour, and a blacksmith who flung his heavy hammer.
“Too slow!” cried the wee bannock, rolling over the brae.
At every cottage someone fancied a bite. A farmer swung a stick. A shepherd threw his bonnet. A hungry family ran after it with their spoons.
The wee bannock rolled into the evening, proud of being quicker than everyone it met.
In the dark it slipped beneath a whin bush to rest—but tumbled straight into a fox’s den.
“Welcome,” said the fox, who had eaten nothing for two days.
Snap! That was the end of the wee bannock’s running.
